verdict.rationale: Jules's docs describe an end-to-end autonomous flow: it clones the repo into a VM, installs dependencies, plans, modifies files, presents a diff and opens a PR. Test writing is supported only by one community user, who says it is good at tests for specific, isolated functions. Other users report weak output and incomplete tasks on more complex work. missing for 10: first-party documentation that Jules writes and runs tests as part of a feature, evidence of reliable end-to-end delivery on complex features.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent implement a requested feature end-to-end, including writing tests

citations.quote: Jules runs in a virtual machine where it clones your code, installs dependencies, and modifies files.
Once you submit a task, Jules will generate a plan. You can review and approve it before any code changes are made.
Jules creates a PR of the changes. Approve the PR, merge it to your branch, and publish it on GitHub.
is good at making tests for very specific/isolated functions
